findings.reason: a worker would either invent a plan_dispatch parameter and thread it through dispatch.py (a scope extension §3 does not declare) or move the refusal to the CLI, contradicting the stated location.
findings.text: §3 says the brief refusal "is a finding in `reckon/crew/node.py` ... and `plan_dispatch` calls it", but `plan_dispatch` (reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:557-584) takes no plan_link or unplanned_reason parameter and the plan forbids a new TaskNode field, so the named caller cannot see whether either flag was given; the real launch runs plan_dispatch from `dispatch()` in reckon/crew/dispatch.py (call at :1670), which is not in §3's declared write paths, so implementing the mechanism as written requires editing dispatch.py outside scope

findings.reason: left as written, the plan moves the check earlier for one of the two roles the landing refusal covers and silently leaves the other where §1 complains it is.
findings.text: §3 refuses only "an implement-role dispatch with `--brief` and no `--plan`", while the landing discharge it mirrors (`_require_brief_owner`, reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:1794) gates on `EXECUTABLE_SECTION_ROLES` = {"implement", "test"} (reckon/evidence.py:277), so a test-role brief run still meets the plan-link request only after the work is done — the exact defect §1 states

response_events.note: §3 now threads plan_link and unplanned_reason from the CLI through dispatch() (dispatch.py near line 1670) into plan_dispatch as parameters, and dispatch.py joins the write paths.
§3 now refuses every role in EXECUTABLE_SECTION_ROLES (implement and test, evidence.py near line 277), the set the landing discharge gates on, with a test-role case.
